title: The Hook
summary: The first 5 to 10 seconds of a told tale decide whether the listener leans in or rocks back. This kit listens for what made a body tip forward.

questions.prompt: Play back the first 10 seconds of your tale. What did you give the listener first — a person, a place, or a problem?
Which of these makes a stronger hook?
options: A boy went to the store.
There were three boys at the store that morning, and only one of them was going home.
Once upon a time, in a kingdom far away…
questions.rationale: Specificity ("three", "that morning") plus stakes ("only one was going home") makes the listener lean in. Lean's body would tip forward at second 5.

questions.prompt: Tell the same tale's hook a second time. Pick one detail that wasn't in the first try and lead with it. Did the energy of the room change?
Take this hook and make it leanable in 12 words or fewer: 'So, um, my dog Otis got into the trash again last weekend.'

castCameos.line: I leaned forward at the second the room got specific. You felt it too.
Hook fast. You had ten seconds and you used eight. Good shape.
A hook is not yet a turn — but it has to promise that a turn is coming.
Whatever short, slightly mysterious phrase your hook used — save it. We'll bring it back at the close.
